A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a set with an [[Definition:Injection|injection]] $\iota: \N \to X$.
Then $X$ is [[Definition:Equinumerous|equinumerous]] with the proper subset $X \setminus \set {\map \iota 0}$; that is, $X$ is [[Definition:Dedekind-Infinite Set|Dedekind-infinite]].

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Successor Mapping|successor mapping]] $n \mapsto n + 1$ is a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] $\N \to \N \setminus \set 0$.

substitutions.N: any set containing a copy of N
substitutions.the successor map: the shift along the copy, extended by the identity

derived.the shifted copy: a bijection onto a proper subset

object_map.reformulation: Shift along an embedded copy of N and fix everything else.

validity_conditions: Injectivity of iota makes the shift well-defined on its image.
With countable choice, every infinite set contains a copy of N, so infinite and Dedekind-infinite coincide.
proof_plan: Define $h: X \to X \setminus \set {\map \iota 0}$ by $\map h {\map \iota n} = \map \iota {n + 1}$ and $\map h x = x$ for $x \notin C$.
On $C$, $h$ is the source bijection transported along $\iota$, so it is a bijection $C \to C \setminus \set {\map \iota 0}$; off $C$ it is the identity.
